previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain, gastroparesis, functional dyspepsia, anxiety, depression, and PTSD was admitted for an acute flare of epigastric pain and nausea, consistent with prior episodes. She was managed with an established inpatient protocol involving initial NPO status, IV fluids, pain control, and gradual dietary advancement. She initially failed a trial of clear liquids but later tolerated a BRAT diet. During the admission, she developed cellulitis at an IV site on her left hand, which was treated with IV ceftriaxone followed by oral Keflex. Her pain and nausea improved, and she was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue her home medications, complete the antibiotic course, and follow up with her PCP and GI specialist.

for oral contrast.

effusion.  The heart size is normal.

weighted sequences.  Arising from the posterior superior aspect of segment VII
is a 3 mm cyst or biliary hamartoma, denoted by high internal signal intensity
on T2 weighted sequences without appreciable internal contrast enhancement
(series 1403, image 29, series 4, image 9).  There is no concerning hepatic
mass.

Biliary: There is no intra or extrahepatic bile duct dilation.  The
gallbladder is normal.  No ductal stones are detected.

Pancreas: Previously-seen mild prominence of the pancreatic duct on the ___ examination has resolved.  This possibly represents resolution of
prior pancreatitis.  The pancreatic parenchyma demonstrates normal bulk and
signal intensity.  There is no focal pancreatic lesion.  There is no
peripancreatic fluid or stranding.

Spleen: The spleen size is normal.  There is no focal splenic lesion.  A 10 mm
accessory spleen is incidentally noted (series 1403, image 59).

Adrenal Glands: The adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

Kidneys: The kidneys are normal in size and enhance symmetrically, without
hydronephrosis.  Arising from the anterior interpolar aspect of the right
kidney is a 5 mm cyst (series 4, image 35).  There is no concerning renal
mass.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  The stomach and intra-abdominal loops of small and
large bowel are normal in caliber.  There is no focal gastrointestinal lesion.

Lymph Nodes: There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

Vasculature: The abdominal aorta, celiac trunk, SMA, and renal arteries are
patent and normal in caliber.  The proximal ___ is patent.  There is an
accessory or replaced left hepatic artery arising from the left gastric
(series 1401, image 40).  The portal and hepatic veins are patent.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: There are no osseous lesions concerning
for malignancy or infection.

IMPRESSION:


1. No MR evidence for pancreatitis. Previously-seen mild pancreatic duct

2. No intra- or extrahepatic bile duct dilation.  Normal gallbladder.
3. Normal MR appearance of the stomach.  Though there are no secondary signs
